featured.title: Yancoal Australia: 10-year forecast and DCF valuation
featured.problem: What is an ASX-listed coal producer worth once its environmental costs are priced in?
featured.data: Yancoal 2024 Annual Report and Sustainability Report; 5 years of historical financials (FY2020–FY2024).
featured.method: Driver-based forecast of sales, EBITDA, capex and net working capital for FY2025–FY2034, discounted at a WACC of 8.25% with 1.5% terminal growth, then adjusted for environmental costs.
featured.result: Equity value of A$17.3bn on a purely financial basis versus A$10.5bn after environmental costs, a 39% gap.

featured.title: 1,200 MW offshore wind farm: investment model

metrics.label: NPV impact of a 5% price move

featured.problem: Is an A$3.6bn offshore wind farm supplying an aluminium smelter financially viable, and what drives its value?
featured.data: Project assumptions: 200 turbines, construction 2025–2028, operation 2029–2058, tariff of A$90/MWh.
featured.method: 30-year cash flow model covering the capex schedule, operations, depreciation and tax; ±5% sensitivity tests on WACC, price and capex; base, best, worst and policy scenarios.
featured.result: Base-case NPV of A$470m, IRR of 7.73% and payback of about 14.5 years. Electricity price is the main value driver.

featured.title: Portfolio analysis and efficient frontier
featured.problem: How should a long-only investor split money across US, international and Vietnamese equities, bonds and gold, and does the 'optimal' mix hold up on data it has not seen?
featured.data: 10 years of daily adjusted prices (2015–2024, 2,515 trading days) for 5 ETFs (SPY, EFA, VNM, AGG, GLD) from Yahoo Finance; T-bill ETF (BIL) as the risk-free rate (1.6% a year).
featured.method: Annualised returns, volatility and correlations in pandas; long-only optimisation with SciPy (maximum Sharpe, minimum variance, efficient frontier); equal-weight and 60/40 benchmarks; out-of-sample test with weights fitted on 2015–2019 and held through 2020–2024.
featured.result: In sample, the maximum-Sharpe mix (54% S&P 500, 46% gold) reached a Sharpe ratio of 0.83 versus 0.66 for 60/40, because gold barely moved with equities (correlation 0.05). Out of sample it fell to 0.19 while 60/40 held 0.53: weights fitted on 2015–2019 put 75% into bonds, which then returned −0.1% a year, including −13% in 2022.

featured.title: Credit card default risk (SQL + Power BI)

metrics.label: Defaults caught by watch list (22.7% flagged)

featured.problem: A card issuer sees about 1 in 5 clients default. Which segments drive defaults, and what should change in collections and limit policy?
featured.data: UCI Default of Credit Card Clients: 30,000 clients of a Taiwanese bank, 6 months of repayment status, bills and payments (2005).
featured.method: SQL (SQLite) to load, clean and engineer features (utilisation, payment ratio, months late); default rates by segment and a status × utilisation risk matrix; Power BI dashboard with DAX measures. Sex and marital status deliberately excluded.
featured.result: Default rate rises from 11.7% for clients never late to 70.3% for clients late in all 6 months. A one-line rule (late this month) flags 22.7% of clients with a 50.3% default rate and catches 51.7% of next-month defaults. Recommendations: start collections on the watch list right away, freeze limit increases after 3+ late months, and encourage paying in full.

more.title: Edu Aegis: AI study-support chatbot
more.problem: Lecturers carry heavy teaching loads while students expect faster, more personal answers, and many students feel uncomfortable using email or the LMS to ask questions.
more.data: Google Forms survey of [TODO: confirm, 186 or about 108] students; interviews with lecturers and teaching assistants at VinUniversity, Brighton College and RMIT; secondary research.
more.approach: Turned survey findings into an MVP feature set (automatic answers from lecture materials, academic-progress alerts, synced reminders, fair group grading) and a two-tier subscription model for universities and training centres.
more.result: About 70% of respondents ask lecturers questions two or more times a week; 50.9% wanted a dedicated tool (20.4% did not). The team reached the Top 10.
more.role: Team Leader of a 4-person team: led the research, problem statement, market analysis and pitch.

more.title: YouTube monetisation analysis
more.problem: Which countries, categories and channel types earn the most on YouTube while overall views decline, and where is the opportunity for a new channel?
more.data: Global YouTube Statistics 2023 (Kaggle): 995 channels with subscribers, views, uploads, category, country and estimated earnings.
more.approach: Cleaned the data in Python (pandas): checked 995 records for missing values, kept 554 complete records and dropped 9 unused columns; built a Power BI dashboard of countries, categories and trends.
more.result: The US, India, Brazil and South Korea led on audience; Entertainment and Music earned the most per video. The team recommended a People & Blogs channel on Vietnamese food aimed at the US, Korea and Russia.
more.role: Data analysis member of a 4-person team: collected, cleaned and processed the data with SQL and Python.

more.title: Production scheduling data pipeline
more.problem: Schedule a factory's operations from raw production data while keeping deliveries on time.
more.data: 989 cleaned rows of manufacturing order and capacity data.
more.approach: Built a modular pipeline for demand analysis, optimisation (JuMP with the HiGHS solver) and KPI evaluation, then tested load-rebalancing scenarios across machines.
more.result: Scheduled 495 of 495 operations (100%) with a 93.9% on-time delivery rate, and raised machine M04 utilisation from 10.6% to 86.6%.

more.title: Fama-French five-factor regression
more.problem: How well do the five Fama-French factors explain an industry's excess returns?
more.data: 14,810 daily observations of industry excess returns and factor returns.
more.approach: Multiple regression, validated with RESET, heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation tests.
more.result: The model explained 76.7% of the variance in excess returns (R² 0.767).
